[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..WvfWv5SXCNLp1t3ykfd2piJ8mF9_XVfgjELbJrMji7I?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=219285119)
Medicaid is a welfare program administered by the states -- a program Jackson voted to expand to able-bodied childless adults and non-citizens as Senate President. Medicare, on the other hand, is a federally administered program that provides health insurance to seniors.
The [hourlong CBS13/FOX23 debate](https://substack.com/redirect/1a22c897-db01-410d-8179-361629043da0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is the first of four televised encounters before the Nov. 3 election. However, early voting has already begun in Maine, with enrolled Democrats disproportionately leading Republicans and unaffiliated voters in requests for absentee ballots.
For Collins, Chair of the powerful Senate Appropriations Committee, it was an opportunity to defend the value of her seniority. For Jackson, the former Maine Senate president who has emphasized his connections to labor unions, it was a chance to persuade voters that Collins would instead use another term to serve Elon Musk and President Donald Trump -- two names that Jackson repeated as if suffering from Tourette syndrome.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/63fbc60d-00a8-4615-9487-1b3b5f580798?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [The Book of Troy: Five Tales from the Maine politics archives...](https://substack.com/redirect/63fbc60d-00a8-4615-9487-1b3b5f580798?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [The Robinson Report](https://substack.com/profile/147548156-the-robinson-report)| | *
---|---|---
| Jul 22
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/63fbc60d-00a8-4615-9487-1b3b5f580798?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Democrats are targeting Collins' seat as they try to win control of the Senate, with Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) directing tens of millions of dollars in ad money and street activist funding to attack Collins and bolster Jackson.
Collins represents a state that Kamala Harris carried in 2024 -- while Trump carried the more conservative Second Congressional District for the third consecutive presidential election, making Maine a unique battleground in the national contest.
If successful, Schumer and his colleagues have made clear that they'd use control of the Senate to lead additional impeachment expeditions against Trump, as well as roll back his immigration policies.
Drawing a sharp contrast with Trump's immigration policies, Schumer even admitted this week that Democrats' goal is to [provide citizenship](https://substack.com/redirect/a4e7667a-e103-44ae-b2b3-d95338e326e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) -- and eventually the right to vote -- to what he estimated as 11 million illegal aliens currently present in the U.S.
In last night's debate, Jackson indicated his opposition to the SAVE Act and state-level voter ID policies, saying that [voters](https://substack.com/redirect/3343bd44-cfe8-4daf-93b3-918dc3a18cfc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) should not have to show ID when casting a vote.
Jackson has had little time to build his Senate campaign.
After losing the Democratic primary for governor, he won the party's July 25 convention to replace Graham Platner, whom Jackson campaigned with as much as he could while seeking the Blaine House.
Platner withdrew from the Senate race amid multiple sexual assault allegations he denied. The switch left Jackson just over 100 days before the election, and he was installed as the nominee without any electoral input from Maine's unenrolled voters.
Collins began the debate with a list of federal investments. As Senate Appropriations Committee chair, she said, she had secured $1.5 billion for 672 Maine projects over five years, including housing, water systems, roads and rural hospitals.
"Effective leadership matters in Washington," she said in her [opening statement](https://substack.com/redirect/b5ef9719-9058-44cb-ab40-58972797ab23?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Jackson used his opening to drop the first of many names he hoped to associate Collins with: Brett Kavanaugh.
"Senator Collins has had 30 years to show whose side she's on," he said.
The fight over affordability followed the same division. Collins blamed policies enacted in Augusta for high electricity rates, housing costs and property taxes. Jackson blamed Trump's tariffs, the Iran war and federal spending decisions, arguing that Collins had done too little to stop them.
"Those are all due to Augusta's failed policies under the failed leadership of Troy Jackson," Collins said of the costs she identified during the affordability exchange.
Jackson repeatedly attacked her role in advancing Trump's 2025 tax-and-spending legislation, which he blamed for cuts to assistance programs. But Jackson appeared to deliberately misrepresent how Collins voted on the so-called One Big Beautiful Bill Act -- a tactic that has also been adopted in many of the Schumer-funded ads airing throughout Maine.
"That's why that bill is crucifying Maine," he said.
Collins supported the [June 28, 2025, motion to begin considering the bill](https://substack.com/redirect/57989e5e-1b7b-47ad-b99d-4354ba10fa1f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), then opposed [final passage July 1](https://substack.com/redirect/dae8b7c6-b4d0-4b51-adbb-91b5d88f317b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). On Tuesday, she said advancing it allowed her to help secure a $50 billion rural health fund. Jackson argued that the fund could not make up for the legislation's harm.
Jackson ran into a more consequential problem when he blamed Collins' long tenure and appropriations chairmanship for inadequate Medicaid payments to Maine hospitals.
"Medicaid rates are set by the state," Collins said.
The [Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services](https://substack.com/redirect/6dc53354-7160-4873-bb3b-4fe9615a313a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) says states establish provider payment rates within federal requirements, with changes subject to federal review. Washington helps finance the program. The appropriations chair does not set Maine's hospital payment schedule.
Jackson also fumbled when he began attacking the role of private equity in buying up single-family housing in Maine, seemingly unaware that Collins had voted in favor of bipartisan legislation to prevent the practice. Rather than course-correct, Jackson doubled down, claiming that, if Collins really had supported such a law, then it wasn't working.
Collins then informed Jackson that the bill was in fact sponsored and co-authored by far-left Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) -- who initially endorsed Graham Platner as "my kind of man" before throwing her support behind Jackson.
Collins also used her opportunity to question Jackson directly to challenge his effectiveness as a legislator. She said more than a third of his bills had been unanimously rejected in committee and asked how he would succeed as the Senate's most junior member.
Jackson said the tally ignored duplicate bills and instances in which he let colleagues advance legislation and receive credit. He disputed Collins' account of the process and insisted she didn't understand how the State Legislature worked.
The debate fell on the eighth anniversary of Collins' confirmation vote, a date Jackson emphasized from his opening statement.
Collins defended judging nominees on their qualifications and pointed to her votes for justices nominated by Democratic presidents. She did not disavow the Kavanaugh confirmation.
[Share The Robinson Report](https://substack..oyIclVVzxkk1Fj0daSe_LfbkU69jQUMEpkP9c58wSDA?)
"I clearly don't agree with how Brett Kavanaugh voted on Roe v. Wade," she said.
Asked directly by WGME moderator Gregg Laggerquist about pay-to-play allegations involving payments made to his lobbyist son, Jackson dodged the question.
Among the pay-to-play allegations facing Jackson is a $50,000 payment to his son Chace Jackson from the Maine Gun Safety Coalition. Less than one month after his son received that contract, Jackson flipped positions he'd held for 20 years on three key pieces of gun control legislation.
"Yeah. Well, I mean, my son, uh, didn't do anything wrong and independent fact checkers have proven that. Uh, time and time again that there was nothing there," he claimed.
Collins then pressed him about the FHA-insured mortgage on his Augusta house. He said he stayed there during the workweek and returned to Allagash on weekends.
In defending false statements he made to acquire the low-interest-rate loan, Jackson may have dug himself a different hole. During the debate, he said that he was working so hard in Augusta that he stayed there five days a week -- which stands in conflict with the mileage reimbursements he received as Senate President.
According to public records obtained under the Freedom of Access Act, Jackson received more reimbursement money during his time as Senate President than any lawmaker in the history of the state.
Collins closed by returning to the argument that has defined her campaign.
"To be effective in the Senate, you need knowledge, experience, seniority and relationships," she said.

Ex-Senate President Troy Jackson, the Democratic replacement for U.S. Senate nominee Graham Platner, appeared to stumbled multiple times in his first of four TV debates with Sen. Susan Collins. Oct 7 | | | | | | | | | | | U.S. Sen. Susan Collins (R) turned her first debate with Graham Platner's replacement into a test of the Democrat ex-Senate President Troy Jackson's record and command of government Tuesday, answering his attacks over President Donald Trump with questions about what Jackson accomplished in Augusta and how he would operate in Washington. Jackson came ready to challenge Collins' vote for Supreme Court Justice Brett Kavanaugh, to which Collins reminded viewers that she'd also voted for Supreme Court Justices Elena Kagan, Sonia Sotomayor, and Ketanji Brown Jackson. Collins attacked Jackson for lying on an application for a Federal Housing Administration (FHA) home loan to get a lower interest rate on a second home he eventually flipped for a roughly $80,000 profit. She also challenged his understanding of Medicaid and Medicare, in an exchange where Jackson appeared to confuse the two programs. [[RELATED: Maine Senate President Troy Jackson Locked in Bitter Legal Fight Over Augusta Home He Bought- and Moved Into - in 2019...]]() Get the investigative news future debates will revolve around first by subscribing to The Robinson Report! Medicaid is a welfare program administered by the states -- a program Jackson voted to expand to able-bodied childless adults and non-citizens as Senate President. Medicare, on the other hand, is a federally administered program that provides health insurance to seniors. The is the first of four televised encounters before the Nov. 3 election. However, early voting has already begun in Maine, with enrolled Democrats disproportionately leading Republicans and unaffiliated voters in requests for absentee ballots. For Collins, Chair of the powerful Senate Appropriations Committee, it was an opportunity to defend the value of her seniority. For Jackson, the former Maine Senate president who has emphasized his connections to labor unions, it was a chance to persuade voters that Collins would instead use another term to serve Elon Musk and President Donald Trump -- two names that Jackson repeated as if suffering from Tourette syndrome. | | | | | | | ---|---|--- | Jul 22 | Democrats are targeting Collins' seat as they try to win control of the Senate, with Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) directing tens of millions of dollars in ad money and street activist funding to attack Collins and bolster Jackson. Collins represents a state that Kamala Harris carried in 2024 -- while Trump carried the more conservative Second Congressional District for the third consecutive presidential election, making Maine a unique battleground in the national contest. If successful, Schumer and his colleagues have made clear that they'd use control of the Senate to lead additional impeachment expeditions against Trump, as well as roll back his immigration policies. Drawing a sharp contrast with Trump's immigration policies, Schumer even admitted this week that Democrats' goal is to -- and eventually the right to vote -- to what he estimated as 11 million illegal aliens currently present in the U.S. In last night's debate, Jackson indicated his opposition to the SAVE Act and state-level voter ID policies, saying that should not have to show ID when casting a vote. Jackson has had little time to build his Senate campaign. After losing the Democratic primary for governor, he won the party's July 25 convention to replace Graham Platner, whom Jackson campaigned with as much as he could while seeking the Blaine House. Platner withdrew from the Senate race amid multiple sexual assault allegations he denied. The switch left Jackson just over 100 days before the election, and he was installed as the nominee without any electoral input from Maine's unenrolled voters. name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Follow the money
disclaimer_text: paid for by the same people cashing in on his administration
body:
How Trump and his administration are benefiting from MAGA donors

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=3046%2E4032634%2ERcgEhU)
---
Want a government job? Need the regulators off your back? Hoping an investigation into your company quietly goes away? In Donald Trump's Washington, there's a way. Write a big check to MAGA Inc., the super PAC he calls: _**"My money that I control."**_ Researchers at the Center for American Progress Action Fund just followed the money, and MAGA Inc. has raised $404.6 million from donors writing checks of $100,000 or more. Of that $404.6 million, 79% came from just 108 donors who got a documented potential benefit from Trump or his administration Simply put: The people bankrolling Trump's super PAC are the same people profiting from his presidency. Here's what that looks like in reality:
* Twenty donors tied to government appointments, for themselves or their relatives and business partners, gave **$87.75 million.**
* Fifty-seven donors who benefited from regulatory rollbacks gave nearly **$82 million.**
* Seven donors who saw enforcement actions against them dropped or reversed gave **$78.6 million.**
* Six donors who've pulled in more than $11 billion in federal contracts, including private prison giant GEO Group, gave **$41.7 million.**
* Two donors connected to presidential pardons gave **$4.5 million.**

The single biggest industry writing checks? Crypto, at **$88.2 million.** Add it all up, and you get pay-to-play on a scale we've never seen. Trump promised to drain the swamp. Instead, he handed it a menu. And while his donors cash in, working families are paying more just to get by. With midterms less than a month away, MAGA Inc. and its spinoff super PACs have reserved $160 million in ads to elect Trump's handpicked candidates, paid for by the same people cashing in on his administration. Trump's big-dollar donors want to believe elections belong to whoever writes the biggest check. They're wrong. They have money. We have people. When we take back control of Congress, we can put real checks on Trump, pass laws to crack down on this kind of self-dealing, and build an America that works for everyone, not just the people who can buy a seat at Trump's gold-plated table. I won't stop fighting until we root out this corruption. Thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth | **Elizabeth Warren is fighting to get Big Money out of politics to make our government work for working families, not just the rich and powerful. And we're doing it with small-dollar, grassroots supporters — not by catering to billionaires or corporations.**

# Four Weeks Until the Election!
---
| |
The Democrat Congressional Campaign Committee just put Washington’s 5th District on its target list and called this race “in play.” That is Washington, D.C., money lining up behind my opponent. We have four weeks to show them it is not in play, and that starts with your vote!
I fought off out-of-state groups in the primary, and I will do it again, because this seat belongs to Eastern Washington, not to national party bosses. We need to stop federal taxes from stacking on top of what Olympia already charges, protect our dams, and keep fighting for fair trade for our farmers and manufacturers.
Your ballot will arrive by October 16th. Confirm your address with [VoteWA.gov](https://us.list-manage.com/12jl1FYuWAo?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238) now, then return your ballot as soon as it shows up! Let’s win this!
---
|
---
| |
# Join Me at the NAACP Candidate Forum
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/bxUo_V_Uh64?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)
| | Click on the picture to reserve your spot today!
---
| | Join me Wednesday, October 14, from 6 to 8 p.m. at the downtown Spokane Public Library, 906 W Main Ave, for the NAACP Spokane Branch Congressional Forum. Ballots drop October 16th! This is one of the last chances for Eastern Washington voters to hear, in person, where I stand and why I am fighting for our jobs, our farms, our families, and our communities. We would love to see you there!
Mark your calendar, tell a friend, and join us at 6 p.m! Admission is free, reserve your ticket by clicking the picture above.
---
|
---
| |
# Night with the Sports Greats
---
|
---
| | Last week we had a great Night With The Sports Greats event with WSU legend Jack Thompson and Gonzaga great Rob Sacre. It was exactly the kind of evening this campaign was built on. The room was full of people who love this district, love their teams, and still make time to show up. Thank you to our wonderful hosts, to our special guests for sharing their time, and to all those who joined us in support.
---
|
---
|
---
| |
# West Plains Chamber of Commerce Candidate Forum
---
|
---
| | My team enjoyed joining the West Plains Chamber of Commerce for their Candidate Forum last week. Senator Mike Padden was kind enough to speak on my behalf. I appreciated him sharing with local businesses and neighbors about the work we are doing for Eastern Washington. From Fairchild and the West Plains economy to the concerns of local employers and families, I fight for you. Thank you to Sen. Padden and to the West Plains Chamber for organizing this great event.
---
|
---
|
---
| |
# An Evening in Dayton,
# Lincoln Dinner
---
|

* * *
The extradition papers for Andrew and Tristan Tate finally dropped, and the accusations against the manosphere influencers with deep ties to Donald Trump's family and administration are horrifying.
These men are human traffickers. They are child porn peddlers. They are abusers of women and kids. The accusations include sexually abusing animals, sexually abusing minors, selling sexually explicit material of minors over WhatsApp, and a long list of other heinous crimes. They should be locked away for a very long time.
It's unbelievable to me that after a decade of this, these two still haven't been thrown in jail. But it shows exactly how the current system works for people with money and power: if you're wealthy enough, connected enough, and influential enough with the right group of people, you can keep outrunning justice and can get away with it. The Tate brothers were taken into custody by U.S. Marshals in July, and more than two months later, they're _still_ _here_ desperately trying to rattle their way out of facing extradition to the UK.
We've seen it with the Tate brothers. We've seen it with Epstein. Epstein was investigated in 2005, only to weasel his way into a sweetheart plea deal and secret non-prosecution agreement that protected him and his co-conspirators -- buying him another _decade_ to traffic and abuse and maybe even kill children before federal prosecutors finally came after him again. An entire decade. And to this day, we still don't even publicly know the identities of everyone who was protected. We saw it with the Wall Street financial crimes of 2008. We've seen it time and time again.
Power buys access. Access buys protection. And protection buys time. Hell, on any given day I wouldn't be surprised if Donald Trump decided to pardon Diddy or Russell Brand or Harvey Weinstein, given how many horrible people he's already let loose by abusing the pardon power the Constitution gives him.
It's maddening. So I'm writing today to repeat my call: every member of Donald Trump's family, every member of his administration, and every Republican influencer, member of Congress, and staffer who manipulated our criminal justice and political systems to give the Tate brothers sanctuary in the United States, so they could shield themselves from the crimes they're accused of in Europe and elsewhere, should be thoroughly investigated by Congress.
That includes Trump's kids, like Don Jr. and Barron. And these relationships go back years. Tate was messaging with Don Jr. and bragging about having access to the president's son long before Trump returned to office. Barron in particular has a close relationship with Andrew Tate, who he took dating advice from. During the 2024 campaign, one of Tate's closest associates got into Mar-a-Lago and helped cultivate a relationship between Tate and Barron. It includes administration officials like Paul Ingrassia, who had to withdraw a Senate-confirmable nomination after text messages surfaced in which he talked about having a Nazi streak. It includes Alina Habba, who went on Benny Johnson's podcast with Andrew Tate and told him, "I'm a big fan," "I admire what you're doing," and, incredibly, "If you're in the States, I got your back". These are people with proximity to power: to the president and the United States government.
And Tate himself seemed to understand exactly what those relationships could mean for him. While he was still stuck in Romania, he posted after Trump's return to power: "The Tates will be free, Trump is the president." Two weeks later, Romania lifted the brothers' travel ban and they flew to the United States.
I want to know the depth of the depravity that made these people think it was appropriate to bring these scumbags to the United States. I want to know how the Tates got one of MAGA's most infamous lawyers to go work for them. And I want to know what role Mar-a-Lago has played in all of this, because these connections keep leading back there. Joe McBride, the Tates' longtime lawyer and a scumbag in his own right, was at Mar-a-Lago when Trump _launched_ his 2024 presidential campaign. Think about that.
And I want to know just how close they've come to being saved from extradition, McBride has been actively lobbying on their behalf, going _back_ to Mar-a-Lago, meeting with Trump administration officials, and desperately trying to get Donald Trump, Marco Rubio, or somebody else in that family or administration to stop the Tate brothers from being extradited to the UK to finally face their crimes.
If this isn't an attempt to influence and corrupt the government of the United States, I don't know what is.
So far, as far as I can tell, Todd Blanche and the Trump DOJ have done the right thing in the extradition process. They fought the brothers' bail. They're moving forward, however slowly.
* * *

Just $8/month makes a huge difference:](https://substack.com/redirect/f93c23b4-fded-4f69-9e34-39f68920ac61?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

* * *
But let me be clear: I'm not giving them a fucking medal for it. I don't believe these people suddenly discovered a moral compass. And I can't help wondering whether, if the British government weren't demanding the Tates back to face charges there, this DOJ would be doing anything at all. After everything we've watched them bury, deflect, and refuse to seriously pursue around Epstein, why should I assume otherwise? Frankly, shipping the Tate brothers off to Britain may be the easiest option they have. Let somebody else's government deal with them. Get them out of the United States. Get the story away from Trump, his family, and the people around him. Make this somebody else's scandal.
Maybe I'm too cynical. But Todd Blanche was Donald Trump's personal criminal defense lawyer before he became Attorney General. So no, I'm not going to assume that doing the right thing here means they're doing it for the right reasons.
But none of that means the outcome is guaranteed. It only takes one person with enough power to step in and Marco Rubio has the power to save the Tate brothers and block their extradition. And after everything we've watched over the last decade, and especially everything we've witnessed this administration corrupt in our country in the last year and a half, I would never, ever bet against these people doing the wrong thing.
That's why it's time for Congress, and eventually a sane, Democratic-run Department of Justice, to get serious about holding these people accountable. We can't keep letting this happen. They abused our government to bring accused human traffickers here because those traffickers endorsed Donald Trump, said nice things about him on the internet, and were friends with the president's kids.
And now they've all gone quiet as church mice. But there are MAGA influencers complicit in this. There are government officials complicit in this. There are Trump family members complicit in this. We have to know the truth. At a bare minimum, the public needs to understand what happened here, because it's emblematic of the much bigger problem.
And here's the part I don't want anyone to lose sight of. Were these people focused on making things less expensive? On helping you buy a house? On ending this war, moving the country forward, or solving any of the many challenges making your life worse and stripping you of your dignity? No. They were too busy doing stupid shit like this. They were too busy getting their friends out of Romania. They were too busy pardoning crooks who'll put money in Donald Trump's back pocket. They were too busy selling out America's national security to foreign governments so Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump could build a private, Epstein-style island off the coast of Albania. This is what they're using their power for.
That's why I'm so laser-focused on the Tate brothers, and on Trump's corruption more broadly. Because the more you look at what happened with the Tates, the more you see the same corruption that runs through everything else Trump and the people around him touch. And it helps explain why nothing is getting done in Washington. They're focused on: self-enrichment, self-indulgence, self-dealing, corruption. All of it. They're so focused on feeding their basest interests, stealing from the American taxpayer, and lining their own pockets that they don't care what crimes their friends commit. They're blinded by proximity to power, influence, and money. It has to stop.
I need the Democratic Party to be ready to take this seriously when we take back Congress. Not with another strongly worded letter. Not with another hearing where everyone gets five minutes to make a viral clip. But with subpoenas, testimony, unredacted documents, and names. The American people are owed real answers and real accountability. And I'm looking forward to watching Barron Trump testify under oath, in public, about his relationship with the Tate brothers and what he knew about their horrendous crimes -- and what he or anyone around Donald Trump did to help them.
Eyes on the ball folks.
With urgency,
--Mike

Dear Fellow Conservative,

Even though we don’t know each other yet, I’m writing to ask you to stand beside me at the top of a very slippery slope.

Actually, in my case, it’s a slippery slide.

Because my name is Riley Gaines and I’m the University of Kentucky swimmer who had to compete against a fully intact 6’4” male swimmer dressed in a women’s bathing suit.

And after he stole the victory I had worked for my entire life, I had to go back to the women’s locker room and undress out of my wet bathing suit while he did the same next to me.

Maybe you want to stop reading right now.

I know the images I’m bringing up are horrible.

But please don’t stop.

Because God-fearing, faith-filled people like you and me have a job to do today.

We can’t retreat into our homes and hope President Trump will fix everything and the Left’s evil culture will just pass us by.

That’s why I’m asking you to give in the next 48 hours.

My fellow conservative, you know this slippery slide.

It’s the same one you got pushed down when the Left told you abortion was going to be “safe, legal, and rare.” Now abortion is a “right” and “women’s healthcare.” And if you don’t support it up until the moment of birth, you must “hate women.”

It’s the same slippery slide you got pushed down when the Left told you limiting gay couples to civil unions was “mean.” You were told, “They just want to use the word “marriage” like everyone else. Join the PA WFP on October 14th to make calls for Mark Pinsley | | | Peter, We want more for Pennsylvania: **schools with the resources our kids deserve, wages that cover the bills, and elected leaders willing to take on the corporations driving up our costs.** Getting there means electing more people who will fight alongside us. This November, **Mark Pinsley’s race for Pennsylvania’s 16th State Senate District** gives us a chance to do that and move closer to flipping the PA Senate. Why does that matter? **Because passing legislation in the House isn’t enough. It has to get through the Senate, too, where the Republican majority can keep bills from ever reaching a vote.** This June, after the House passed a bill to raise the minimum wage to $15 an hour, Senate Republicans _blocked_ an effort to bring it to the floor. Who controls the Senate helps determine whether the things we’re fighting for become law or stay stuck in Harrisburg. Flipping it would give us a path to move those priorities forward and a new majority to organize and hold accountable. **Mark is running for a Republican-held seat in Senate District 16 on fully funded public schools, affordable health care, stronger worker protections, and lower utility bills.** A win would mean another advocate for working people in Harrisburg and one fewer seat in the Republican majority standing in the way of progress. To help Mark win, we need to make sure voters hear what he’s fighting for and turn out to support him. That’s where you come in. # [18.4 cents off every gallon? Trump says he is thinking about it](https://substack.com/redirect/b4b43971-f24e-4b58-819d-cad8c8c1f235?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
President Trump said Tuesday he is **["thinking about"](https://substack.com/redirect/a1751f53-6fad-43c5-bf51-2c8220ad6fd3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** suspending the 18.4-cent federal gasoline tax, as regular averaged $4.36 a gallon, up from $3.13 a year earlier.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b4b43971-f24e-4b58-819d-cad8c8c1f235?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **No plan attached:** He took the question at Anduril Industries in Sparrow Point, Maryland, and gave no further detail on timing or scope. The 18.4-cent figure is the Energy Information Administration's federal gasoline tax.
* **Hormuz, then refineries:** On Oct. 6 he said Hormuz flows were "even and sometimes exceeding" prewar levels. An Oct. 5 Truth Social post blamed refineries, citing Russian plants hit by Ukraine and closures in blue states including California.
* **Diesel order already out:** An Oct. 5 executive order expands red-dyed diesel access, directs penalty relief for highway use, and reviews whether the diesel tax can be deferred through Dec. 31. He put the trucker saving at about $100 a fill-up.
* **Pushback on the cause:** Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Oct. 4 the strait stays shut until summer-deal conditions are met.

# [SpaceX is borrowing $40 billion to buy Nvidia chips](https://substack.com/redirect/b4b43971-f24e-4b58-819d-cad8c8c1f235?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
SpaceX is seeking about[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/5f86a48b-1ad7-4acf-b59d-9d982b5ba8b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[$40 billion through an Apollo-led,](https://substack.com/redirect/5f86a48b-1ad7-4acf-b59d-9d982b5ba8b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/5f86a48b-1ad7-4acf-b59d-9d982b5ba8b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)chip-backed vehicle to fund what the Financial Times called a "blockbuster" Nvidia order, 16 weeks after a record IPO.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b4b43971-f24e-4b58-819d-cad8c8c1f235?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Loan and bond split:** ZeroHedge, citing the FT, said the raise is roughly $10 billion in bank loans and $30 billion in investment-grade debt, in a "Project Beignet"-like vehicle collateralized by chips.
* **IPO and bonds:** June's IPO raised $86 billion, and SpaceX sold $25 billion of investment-grade bonds less than two weeks later. The new talks come less than four months after trading began.
* **Exclusive hardware:** **[Barron's reported](https://substack.com/redirect/b32c6af1-8d4d-417d-974a-6ada9dbd3dad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Musk has praised Jensen Huang and said SpaceX will use only Nvidia hardware, and that the company is preparing to spend **[tens of billions on that equipment.](https://substack.com/redirect/5c87c118-078b-479f-b74c-d73306af464f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
* **Starlink and Grok:** Investor's Business Daily said the chip reports came Tuesday, as SpaceX won approval **[to launch 15,000 more satellites for Starlink](https://substack.com/redirect/48cc48f1-3238-4d9c-9c87-e40aff6e7aaf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/48cc48f1-3238-4d9c-9c87-e40aff6e7aaf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)Mobile. # [IMF to paralyzed France: Get your house in order](https://substack.com/redirect/b4b43971-f24e-4b58-819d-cad8c8c1f235?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Kristalina Georgieva used a Singapore interview to tell Paris **[the books have to be tightened,](https://substack.com/redirect/0cf3f2e7-8535-4c20-9087-f3346f97dab8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/0cf3f2e7-8535-4c20-9087-f3346f97dab8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)with campus unrest now in week three and investors demanding more yield on French 10-year debt than on Italian debt after a climb of more than 100 basis points this year.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b4b43971-f24e-4b58-819d-cad8c8c1f235?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Her warning:** In Singapore, Georgieva told CNBC that France had borrowed "shock after shock after shock," "climbing on this staircase that does not lead to heaven." She added, "get your house in order."
* **Deficit path:** She said there is "a very clear recognition" the deficit must come under 5%. It was 5.1% of GDP last year. France is in the EU excessive-deficit procedure, which uses a 3% reference.
* **Protests and budget:** Nationwide student protests, which have turned violent, are in a third week. Paris is starting budget talks and seeking cuts worth tens of billions of euros.
* **Not 2012, she said:** Georgieva said the economy is growing and Europe now has the European Central Bank plus other stability tools. "Bond markets respond to fundamentals," she said, with inflation, rates, and debt all higher.

# [Porsche will cut 9,000 jobs as margins fell from 18% to 1%](https://substack.com/redirect/b4b43971-f24e-4b58-819d-cad8c8c1f235?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Porsche's Wednesday restructuring would **[remove roughly 9,000 positions, about a fourth of the company,](https://substack.com/redirect/3c2172b0-4e34-4222-b5dc-28abf8c8993d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on a timetable running to 2030, after a first-half China volume drop of nearly one-third and a margin that fell to 1.1%.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b4b43971-f24e-4b58-819d-cad8c8c1f235?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Cuts could go further:** The company said the reductions, some already announced, could reach 30%. Last year's profit margin was 1.1%, down from 18% two years earlier. Chief Executive Michael Leiters presented the plan, Sportwagenschmiede '35, at Weissach.
* **Fewer cars, higher prices:** Porsche wants the average price of top-end models up about 20% in the medium term and model variants down about 20%. Development costs are targeted down as much as 20%, production personnel costs as much as 30%, and management posts by 40%.
* **China is the hole:** The New York Times puts first-half China volumes down nearly a third. At the peak China was more than a third of sales. By 2030 that share is expected near 1 in 10. Leiters said a return to those levels "at any cost" would not be "realistic or beneficial."
* **Parent takes the hit:** Volkswagen owns 75% of Porsche and earlier this year approved a group plan for 100,000 job cuts and a 9% margin by 2030. The Times tied Porsche's slide to a €6 billion write-down last month and about €700 million in U.S. tariff costs last year.

Parent takes the hit: Volkswagen owns 75% of Porsche and earlier this year approved a group plan for 100,000 job cuts and a 9% margin by 2030. name: Molly Gray
subject: Housing is on the ballot this November
body:
Hi Peter, This campaign has been and will always be about the issues facing Vermonters- and right now, **people across this state are struggling to pay for housing.** Whether it’s rent, mortgage, or property taxes, Vermonters today are giving up an unsustainable amount of their income just to keep a roof over their heads. So today, I want to talk about how we can build and rehab more homes that Vermonters can actually afford– and in the process, help to make sure Vermont is a place where businesses can recruit and retain talent. I have a specific, actionable housing plan. You can [read all five parts here](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140892767/651857543/-1662054583?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4N2NmZDI0MC03NmMyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=U03GIRTH4AmNMtjc08AxL_gVNE-0EUOMn6Ay5LypslA=&emci=96906505-74c2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=87cfd240-76c2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=43402276) and read a recent [commentary of mine here](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140892768/651857544/-1134821309?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4N2NmZDI0MC03NmMyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=U03GIRTH4AmNMtjc08AxL_gVNE-0EUOMn6Ay5LypslA=&emci=96906505-74c2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=87cfd240-76c2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=43402276) but today I want to focus on two sections: **cutting red tape in municipal zoning codes, and growing our housing work force.** Last week [I talked about my support from the Vermont model code](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140892770/651857545/-620777322?si=GUKrjMpO1CTof7XH&t=1836&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4N2NmZDI0MC03NmMyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=U03GIRTH4AmNMtjc08AxL_gVNE-0EUOMn6Ay5LypslA=&emci=96906505-74c2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=87cfd240-76c2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=43402276). Having a lightweight, easy-to-navigate municipal zoning code gives builders predictability and reduces permitting delays, which can add thousands to any project. A model zoning code is also a [great option for towns left behind by Act 181](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140892771/651857546/-1793334511?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4N2NmZDI0MC03NmMyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=U03GIRTH4AmNMtjc08AxL_gVNE-0EUOMn6Ay5LypslA=&emci=96906505-74c2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=87cfd240-76c2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=43402276), allowing them to benefit from reduced Act 250 oversight. Finally, we cannot build the homes Vermonters need without workers. That’s why I’m proposing the Vermont Housing Corps: the next generation of skilled tradespeople such as carpenters, electricians, and plumbers. We can create more apprenticeships by matching students in Vermont’s career and technical education centers with employers who need workers. We can help students launch their careers with scholarships, loan forgiveness, and tax credits for those who commit to working in Vermont’s home construction industries– something we already do for college and university students. I call this initiative the Vermont Housing Corps, and it can help Vermont fill important gaps in our workforce while rapidly building the housing we need. _-Molly Gray_ P.S. **President Trump’s decisive re-election in 2024 was more than a political comeback — it was a national gut-check. A repudiation of the corrupt ruling class. A mandate to finally take back control of our country.

Not $100. Not $50. Not even $25!

Just $15.

Friend, it's Michele Tafoya. I'm sure you've received plenty of political messages this time of year from thankless politicians who have spent the majority of their careers in Washington, lining their own pockets.To be candid with you, that's everything I'm NOT.
I spent the better part of my life on the sidelines watching the best athletes in the world compete at the highest level.
I know what it takes to be a winner, I've seen it firsthand.That's the pedigree I've brought to this campaign.
Not cutting corners, not cheating myself, or letting my team down.
But I can't be the only one bought in if we're going to succeed this fall, Friend.

It's going to take a group of us going the extra mile to create change.

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: This poll changes everything
body:
49–46.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, look at this:
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261007_2_nyt.KfgDlA&refcode=em20261007-2353&amount=5&t=1&akid=2353%2E299639%2ErJmw6U)
In June, the _New York Times_ /Siena poll had me trailing Greg Abbott by 7 points, 51% to 44%.
**Now, that same poll has me ahead, 49% to 46%.**
That's a 10-point swing in three months, from one of the most respected pollsters in the country. It's not a fluke, either. This is the fourth poll showing us ahead of Abbott after weeks of Abbott's attack ads flooding Texas airwaves. **[Chip in $5 right now to help us turn this polling lead into a win.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261007_2_nyt.KfgDlA&refcode=em20261007-2353&amount=5&t=2&akid=2353%2E299639%2ErJmw6U)**
The _New York Times_ also ran a major story this weekend on the state of play in Texas. Read this:
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261007_2_nyt.KfgDlA&refcode=em20261007-2353&amount=5&t=3&akid=2353%2E299639%2ErJmw6U)
**Ten-to-one. Abbott has thrown everything he has at this race, and he still can't put it away.**
Wendy Davis put it this way in the same article: "People have vastly underestimated Gina. Dollar for dollar, she's running the best statewide campaign we've ever seen."
That's what grassroots supporters like you have built $5 and $10 at a time. We haven't come close to matching Abbott's money, but every dollar has gone further than anyone thought it could. **[Will you make your first contribution today to help us keep our momentum going in the final stretch?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261007_2_nyt.KfgDlA&refcode=em20261007-2353&amount=5&t=5&akid=2353%2E299639%2ErJmw6U)**
The Times was also honest about what still stands in our way. Texas has 20 separate media markets, and national donors routinely pass the state over because reaching all of them is so expensive. And one in five Texas voters still doesn't know who I am.
Here's what the last three months have taught us: the more Texans get to know me, the more this race moves. **Every one of those voters is someone we can reach, but only if we have the resources to do it.** Abbott has raised more than $106 million in this race, and he's going to keep spending it in the final month to drag this race back his way.
We are 27 days from Election Day. The polls tell us this race can be won. What happens next depends on whether we have the financial resources to communicate our message to the voters who need to hear it.
**[Can you chip in $5 right now to help us reach every voter in every corner of Texas and defeat Greg Abbott on November 3rd?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261007_2_nyt.KfgDlA&refcode=em20261007-2353&amount=5&t=6&akid=2353%2E299639%2ErJmw6U)**
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261007_2_nyt.KfgDlA&amount=5&refcode=em20261007-2353&t=25&akid=2353%2E299639%2ErJmw6U)
For 32 years, Texans have been told a Democrat can't win statewide. A 10-point swing after more than $70 million in spending against us says otherwise. Let's go take Texas back.
Thank you — for everything,
Gina

name: Troy Jackson
subject: blown away
body:
|
#
| | | | | Hi, Peter – Roy Cooper here. My friend Troy Jackson is running for U.S. Senate in Maine, and he needs our support. If you can, [**_I hope you'll split a donation between our grassroots campaigns._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/19797?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1698&amount=5&t=7&akid=4339%2E124072%2EammWdG)

If you'd no longer like to receive these partner emails, [**_you can opt out here._**](https://act.roycooper.com/signup/unsub-tandems/?t=8&akid=4339%2E124072%2EammWdG)
---|---
Peter, I’m blown away.**
Just as I wrapped up my debate, my staff told me the good news: **you helped us raise $170,000 just while I was on stage?!** _I can’t thank you enough – really._
They said they were aiming for $200,000, but fell just short. I told them it wouldn’t be a problem – that Peter would help us get over the finish line. [**_So before I go on, do you think you can spare a couple of bucks, split between our campaign and Roy Cooper, to help us reach our goal before midnight? A recent poll shows us down by 3 points, so your support would mean a lot to me right now._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/19797?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1698&amount=5&t=9&akid=4339%2E124072%2EammWdG)
| | [GIVE ANY AMOUNT
RIGHT NOW →](https://act.roycooper.com/go/19798?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1698&amount=5&t=10&akid=4339%2E124072%2EammWdG)
---
I have to tell you, Susan Collins gave the exact performance I had expected. Lies, false promises, and a whole lot of concern.
And when I reminded her that **yesterday was the anniversary of her deciding vote to confirm Brett Kavanaugh to the Supreme Court,** and gave her the chance to explain the decision, she showed no regret whatsoever. _Millions of women across the country lost their reproductive rights because of that vote._
Peter, I’ll tell you the same thing that I just told thousands of undecided Mainers: I’m for Medicare-for-all, making billionaires pay their fair share and bringing down the cost of living.
Susan Collins also told those undecided Mainers what she’s for: tax breaks for billionaires and continuing to vote with Donald Trump 96% of the time.
We can defeat Susan in less than a month from now, but I can’t take on this fight alone. **We have been out-spent on TV ads by a 2-to-1 margin! And there’s more cash to come before Election Day.**
[**_So please, if you were waiting for the perfect day to donate, I hope you’ll make today that day. Your $5 right now would help us reach our fundraising goal and flip the Senate._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/19797?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1698&amount=5&t=11&akid=4339%2E124072%2EammWdG)

Troy

name: Eric Pratt
subject: Minnesota doesn't need another career politician
body:
I spent 30 years in the private sector stopping fraud. Here is my plan for Congress.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/14bgkw3181r?e=905d578f8e&c2id=16eb929e7cba591464984f29a5a61342)
| | | | | | ,

**Minnesota doesn't need another career politician.**
Before serving in the Minnesota Senate, I spent decades in the banking industry protecting consumers and fighting financial fraud. I didn't go into politics to make headlines, I went to get common-sense results.
Now, with early voting underway across Minnesota's Second District, Washington needs more experienced problem-solvers and fewer professional politicians.
---
| [WILL YOU STAND WITH ME TODAY? >>](https://us.list-manage.com/I7ssWa1b4P7?e=905d578f8e&c2id=16eb929e7cba591464984f29a5a61342)

| | | | | | | | | | | |

We are facing radical D.C. spending, rising inflation, and out-of-state special interest groups trying to buy this seat. I run this campaign with the exact same fiscal discipline, transparency, and accountability I brought to the private sector.
**If you are ready for steady leadership and practical solutions, our field operations need your backing right now.**

"America will never be a communist country; we will defeat communism, socialism, and Marxism in America once and for all." President Donald Trump
**Destination Reached: How the Long March Ended at City Hall**
On August 24, 1954, President Dwight Eisenhower signed the Communist Control Act, formally outlawing the Communist Party USA and declaring membership in it an act of conspiracy against the United States. The law still sits in the U.S. Code at 50 U.S.C. §§ 841-844\. It has never been repealed outright.
And yet on January 1, 2026, Zohran Mamdani -- a Democratic Socialists of America member elected in November 2025 -- took the oath of office as mayor of the largest city in America. Nobody invoked the law. Nobody could. The seventy-two-year-old statute is a museum piece, and the reason it is a museum piece is the best evidence available that the "long march through the institutions" has, in fact, arrived at its destination.

We’ll get right to it. **Below are three reasons why we need your help right away.**
1. **Polls and election experts agree: This is anyone’s race to win.** Chris Pappas and John Sununu are neck-and-neck in the polls, and our race is rated a Toss Up.

---
Friend, did you see the news?! Former President Barack Obama just showed his support for my campaign!
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17387?refcode=jtk1471-fr-nd&t=2&akid=13052%2E400544%2E4BYPzm)
| | [Join President Obama in Supporting My Campaign](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17387?refcode=jtk1471-fr-nd&t=3&akid=13052%2E400544%2E4BYPzm)
---
Friend, this moment means more to me than I can say. President Obama and I were both Organizers, and I got my start knocking thousands of doors in Indian Country for his campaign. I was inspired by the belief that we could come together and make a real difference. That experience set me on a path of fighting for New Mexicans and making sure every voice is heard. Today, that same fierce commitment to New Mexico and its people is at the heart of everything I do.

I have traveled across New Mexico to rural and urban counties, from Lovington to Gallup, not just the three times on this campaign but even before that. I know how important it is to just show up and listen to communities who feel that their voices don’t get the attention they deserve.
As I’ve listened to hundreds of thousands of New Mexicans, their priorities have become clear, and so is my commitment to fighting for them: to lower costs and put more money in our pockets, make our streets safer and protect our loved ones from fentanyl, keep our hospitals open and recruit doctors and nurses so we aren’t driving hours for care, create a public option so we aren’t facing thousands of dollars in medical bills, make it easier to get homegrown New Mexican food onto grocery store shelves, protect SNAP, WIC and Medicaid so we have support when we need it, and stop private equity from coming into New Mexico and putting profits over people.

I've spent my entire career working to protect our communities and our culture, friend — and now, I'm ready to deliver as Governor. **_But I can't do it alone._**
With early voting officially open, I am truly honored to have President Obama’s support in this final stretch of the race — and we need to keep building on this momentum to secure our win in November. **Please, will you join former President Obama in supporting my campaign for Governor of New Mexico?[_I've set a goal to raise $15,000 before midnight tonight: friend, will you chip in $5 or more right now?_](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17387?refcode=jtk1471-fr-nd&t=4&akid=13052%2E400544%2E4BYPzm)**

If you don't have time to hear my whole pitch, here's my ask: [**Will you join me in the fight for our future by donating $7 _(generously matched to $21)_ to help my friends at the DSCC take back the Senate for Democrats?**](https://go.dscc.org/go/24256?amount=7&t=5&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&addr1=&addr2=&city=Cresco&state=Pennsylvania&zip=18326&phone=None&employer=&occupation=&ask=7&amounts=7%2C14%2C28%2C70&code=DPE-FD-20261007-MartinSheen-WhatASKMeans2026RF-Pros-sl1&refcode=DPE-FD-20261007-MartinSheen-WhatASKMeans2026RF-Pros-sl1&akid=26598%2E9716520%2EWIJZTc)

Whether they succeed is, in part, up to you.

Flipping the Senate and bringing accountability to this administration _will_ make a difference, but it will only be possible if we lock hands, raise our voices, and come together ‐‐ that's when we can accomplish truly incredible things.

And yet they are running the most radical, well-funded Senate candidates in states across this country who are counting on Republicans to stay home and let them walk right in. body:
| Wow, I’m blown away.

Just as I wrapped up my debate, my staff told me the good news: **you helped us raise $170,000 just while I was on stage?!**_I can’t thank you enough – really._

They said they were aiming for $200,000, but fell just short. I told them it wouldn’t be a problem – that you would help us get over the finish line. [So before I go on, do you think you spare a couple of bucks, split between our campaign and the Voter Protection Project, to help us reach our goal before midnight? A recent poll shows us down by 3 points, so your support would mean a lot to me right now.](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/136608?t=6&akid=29690%2E878179%2Ea-Fpwc) | [GIVE ANY AMOUNT RIGHT NOW →](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/136608?t=7&akid=29690%2E878179%2Ea-Fpwc)
---
I have to tell you, Susan Collins gave the exact performance I had expected. Lies, false promises, and a whole lot of concern.

And when I reminded her that **yesterday was the anniversary of her deciding vote to confirm Brett Kavanaugh to the Supreme Court** , and gave her the chance to explain the decision, she showed no regret whatsoever. _Millions of women across the country lost their reproductive rights because of that vote._

Look, I’ll tell you the same thing that I just told thousands of undecided Mainers: I’m for Medicare-for-all, making billionaires pay their fair share and bringing down the cost of living.

Susan Collins also told those undecided Mainers what she’s for: tax breaks for billionaires and continuing to vote with Donald Trump 96% of the time.

We can defeat Susan in less than a month from now, but I can’t take on this fight alone. **We have been out-spent on TV ads by a 2-to-1 margin! And there’s more cash to come before Election Day.**

[So please, if you were waiting for the perfect day to donate, I hope you’ll make today that day. Your $10 right now would help us reach our fundraising goal and flip the Senate.](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/136608?t=8&akid=29690%2E878179%2Ea-Fpwc)

subject: I support tough, upfront restrictions on data centers:

body:
Without strong guardrails, the costs of building and running these facilities can be passed on to ordinary ratepayers
| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140895629/651866141/-201694504?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxNjYyZWE3ZC03Y2MyLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=fLLZsehqbFtzb5iOmUT0EDaOxUtwZ0afXrl_PSnFrb0=&emci=cc4eb177-7cc2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=1662ea7d-7cc2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=9494239)
---

| | Data centers are expanding across the country, including here in the Pacific Northwest. This growth carries real consequences for our communities. **Data centers require enormous amounts of electricity and water to operate.** Without strong guardrails, the costs of building and running these facilities can be passed on to ordinary ratepayers through higher electricity bills and increased strain on local water systems. At the same time, the public infrastructure that supports our communities, including the power grid, roads, bridges, and schools, requires significant investment. Data center development should strengthen these systems, not strain them. **Last month, I joined 110 House Democrats in a letter to tech industry leaders demanding that data center construction follow strict guardrails to protect consumers.** In that letter, we stated that data center projects must be built and operated responsibly, with high-quality construction, good jobs, strong environmental stewardship, and genuine partnerships with the communities they serve. We also stated that we would oppose new data center projects that fail to include strong labor standards, community benefits agreements negotiated with local leaders, and meaningful steps to protect local air quality, drinking water, and utility costs for residents.**Developers must invest responsibly in grid infrastructure so that ratepayers do not bear the cost of powering these projects.** Next, I voted for the Ratepayers Protection Act, legislation designed to protect families from higher electricity bills caused by data centers in their communities. I am also a cosponsor of the Big Ugly Tax Breaks for Data Centers Act, which would roll back tax breaks for large AI data centers included in Republicans' Big Ugly Law. **Finally, let me make this clear. I support tough, upfront restrictions on data centers, including:**
* No high electric bills for local families and small businesses
* No federal tax breaks
* No construction without community approval and union labor
* Data centers must pay their fair share to connect to and use the grid
* Data centers must use closed-loop water systems

**These bills are only a start, and there is a lot more work to do.** Skagit County and Snohomish County have recently enacted temporary data center moratoriums. I support the ability of local jurisdictions to give themselves time to decide how they want to manage large data centers.**I will keep working to understand how our communities could be impacted by the growth of data centers in the Pacific Northwest.** More soon, _Rick_ | Express Donate: If you've stored your info with ActBlue Express, we'll process your contribution to Rick Larsen instantly:

subject: 💪🏽When students organize, we win. Join us in launching Powered by Students
body:
Our generation is under attack, and students are stepping up. | | | Peter, Student organizers recently gathered at American University with a message we all deserve to hear: college is for all of us, and immigration status should never decide who gets to learn. Students have always been on the frontline of change. From fighting for in-state tuition, even in some of the reddest states in the country, to winning DACA, which opened the door to higher education for hundreds of thousands of immigrant youth, when students organize, we win. Now our generation is under attack. Students are facing a wave of attacks that make college harder to afford and push it further out of reach. The federal government has sued all 21 states that offer in-state tuition to undocumented students that grew up in their states. Many of us are already working multiple jobs and carrying tens of thousands of dollars in debt just to stay in class. **This is why we’re launching the Powered by Students Campaign, to bring students together on their campuses to build the skills and relationships to organize and win.** **[READY TO START ORGANIZING?](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.v2UrIOJHHKkg0Pk-aGvhyzCKAdQv6ANAIbZ_2K5v_dCxap16cuNelliFkKKa9dnwuTgiiQWG2353OHQZ6ACCfIc1sDRelra4h_F60beJBuQjtMt5z2kb4-QBW3eTxDraGWBzuqCQaN9Kzqq6_aHTzPWpG0M2YNadqCgUgn4fTJ076qijcVgYX6kjN-vkrebfdO8-yi6l5vA02fSVk0ywZ-xvR4jOGIgSvNelXbglPxGBOcksgVlKebmoq8rvYKKjmtRA-fTMyAG2rFT1WIsQFd2qz6hIl2uvAvFZvBd2dD_DNAQ9qSR7BhQenqdiCYFOZ218Cg5v0Aq5yIRnfXVTcprmXuXgMqcz23OXt0UByV8/4uo/N2or6u87TpSnztSge_5h5Q/h0/h001._g0tGbZag-jeUF8ZU02vlYi_zcAcuM3kWU00aD-Tm98)** **** [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.v2UrIOJHHKkg0Pk-aGvhyzCKAdQv6ANAIbZ_2K5v_dCxap16cuNelliFkKKa9dnwuTgiiQWG2353OHQZ6ACCfIc1sDRelra4h_F60beJBuQjtMt5z2kb4-QBW3eTxDraDx-TDx7NbjfdkhWYQRuAgtSkNb9w35SqAsPMh44EBcOXBL2pPFn8qB_SqMvW8NXqdQkQuTBM2b8_TDN3EmQmJOo7vnnfVEil2OC3uX1T0Pff44dOV59BdPUapOscUy9RdAb78VW-8EYortJK9qsH6YtgYFwcPUIC-xH5KflzeGqxboufEAxfZ1nruJ1p_73dXRGybsMMxgxM1uv6UFzvGZoqzq3PrKVTeLEaoilEVA4/4uo/N2or6u87TpSnztSge_5h5Q/h1/h001.0Bzil-a4kqvpTJjeoYyU0I3IzTV9mH6TerK-y25aSgY) [**Ready to find your organizing home?**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.v2UrIOJHHKkg0Pk-aGvhyzCKAdQv6ANAIbZ_2K5v_dCxap16cuNelliFkKKa9dnwuTgiiQWG2353OHQZ6ACCfIc1sDRelra4h_F60beJBuQjtMt5z2kb4-QBW3eTxDraUGHQ9LEQoHt7El_iUEFfG9UtNK_IBkL7kS8qH-viBlprX8DvZR76sX-bdOt2GoI8ZUJSDrvOqlU2OIuagUv_CRuUCnJRVVw2HaGp7SBq1fseBDuedt6SN3ljRGKfL_6tjFx9rv-Br9VfhMlFbxh3Z4oipIR1MwOvx4a5PxLfwJiBc_9ZYF0Pvn0folhSzRvY1MAIBESrCUMvu5DhYaUpuFECrZM3SoOG8xovMs_OpbY/4uo/N2or6u87TpSnztSge_5h5Q/h2/h001.V5hkpxL88U5gB2JsgbJgTc-POjyFSSr4ZFtbq4gLyG0) If you’re new to organizing or not sure where to begin, join a monthly Welcome Call to meet the community and learn your next steps. clean_body: Our generation is under attack, and students are stepping up. | | | Peter, Student organizers recently gathered at American University with a message we all deserve to hear: college is for all of us, and immigration status should never decide who gets to learn. Students have always been on the frontline of change. From fighting for in-state tuition, even in some of the reddest states in the country, to winning DACA, which opened the door to higher education for hundreds of thousands of immigrant youth, when students organize, we win. Now our generation is under attack. Students are facing a wave of attacks that make college harder to afford and push it further out of reach. The federal government has sued all 21 states that offer in-state tuition to undocumented students that grew up in their states. Many of us are already working multiple jobs and carrying tens of thousands of dollars in debt just to stay in class. This is why we’re launching the Powered by Students Campaign, to bring students together on their campuses to build the skills and relationships to organize and win. ** If you’re new to organizing or not sure where to begin, join a monthly Welcome Call to meet the community and learn your next steps. If you’re ready to lead, join one of our teams (event leads, storytelling, texting, and more) , or you can start a campus chapter to bring students together and we’ll provide resources and guidance so you can organize around the issues that matter most to your community. Ready to join young people around the country in fighting for a future for us all? Check out below to learn more about the Powered by Students Campaign and and how you can get active 🗣️ – Aria and the rest of the UWD Team ** | Follow us on: | | | | |

name: Governor Phil Scott
subject: Economic Growth Must Be Our Priority
body:
Economic Growth Must Be Our Priority |
---
| |
---
| **Economic Growth Must Be a Priority**
Dear Friends -

_**In order to make Vermont more affordable we must grow our economy**_.

My team has gained ground in this area (without a lot of support from the legislature), the job is far from over, but the roadmap is clear:

We must build more housing, cut the red tape, stop trying to solve every problem by raising taxes and fees; reform education and health care to lower costs; invest in infrastructure and downtowns across the state; and strengthen our workforce.

**These aren’t radical ideas. This is a commonsense approach that’s been proven time and time again.**

Growth in the economy improves the everyday lives of Vermonters. That’s why it’s been my focus for my many years of public service.

**Today, that basic principle is being challenged**.

When asked whether Vermont should move _away_ from economic growth as a priority, my opponent responded:

[“Yeah, I mean, honestly, I don't think it's that hard because everybody's struggling so much economically.”](https://us.list-manage.com/_GUSgfwm1h6?e=19cebfe173&c2id=84d1094b3a168b6495ef78aca9f3540c)

**_Now... I’m NOT an economist, but my 35 years in business has taught me that when an economy stops growing— or shrinks — it’s called a recession..._

That hurts working families the hardest: jobs become less secure, household incomes stagnate or fall, tax burdens sometimes increase, public services come under pressure, and young families leave in search of opportunity elsewhere.**

Abandoning our work to grow the economy is not the answer... because a healthy economy lifts all boats.

So... I need your help and your vote. To finish the job we started—to grow the economy, attract more business, help the businesses who are here be able to stay; build more housing, get a handle on property taxes and health care costs, and become a more affordable place to live, work and raise a family.

**But I can’t do it alone, which is why my team and I are asking for your support over the next 28 days. You can reach out to us at[www.philscott.org](https://us.list-manage.com/lSVRy0jCEcr?e=19cebfe173&c2id=84d1094b3a168b6495ef78aca9f3540c) to request a lawn sign or volunteer and you can make a contribution by clicking the link below.**

Sincerely,

Governor Scott

clean_body: Newsom signed a law to stop me The dubbed "Stop Nick Shirley Act" was made to stop me. | | | | | | | Friend, There's now a law in California with my name associated with it. Everyone in Sacramento knows exactly what the "Stop Nick Shirley Act" means. On August 22nd, Governor Newsom signed AB 2624. Three days later, I was standing at the State Capitol with a crowd of people who showed up because they understood what this law actually does. Supporters say it protects immigration workers from harassment. Here's what it really does, Friend: it makes it harder for anyone -- me included -- to investigate where your tax dollars are being sent. I said it plainly at the rally: this is not the end; this is just the beginning. Because here's the part that should bother you more than anything else. The assemblymember who wrote this bill is married to California's Attorney General -- the one person in this state whose entire job is supposed to be going after fraud. Instead, his wife wrote the bill that makes it harder to expose it. That's not a coincidence, Friend. That's the system protecting itself. I've spent the last year showing up where legacy media won't -- daycare centers, tax-funded nonprofits, the offices of people who'd rather I disappear than answer a question. That work is exactly why a state legislature decided to write a law with my name on it instead of going after the fraud I keep finding. A state senator at the rally called it unconstitutional. A city attorney called it a direct threat to the First Amendment. They're right -- and they're not going to be the ones who stop it. That's going to take people willing to fund the reporters still asking the questions. Here's something most people don't see, Friend: doing this work independently means there's no network paying for the flight to Sacramento, no legal department covering me if a state files a complaint over a story, no corporate budget for the cameras and editors it takes to get this footage in front of you. When I showed up at that rally, Lincoln Media Foundation was on site with their own journalists to cover it, because they understood what was actually at stake before most of the country did. That 's why I'm partnering with Lincoln Media Foundation. They understand how important it is to support independent journalists and help us keep doing the work without compromising what makes it independent in the first place. I'm grateful for their partnership and commitment, and - helping cover travel, equipment, and the costs that come with confronting people on camera instead of reading a press release about them. Since LMF is a 501(c)3, your gift is tax-deductible , and it can be made anonymously if that's what you'd prefer. Friend, they can pass all the laws they want. They can try to prevent people like me from exposing their corruption, that's why it crucial to support independent journalists like myself. They are creating laws to silence free speech -- and that's why we need to continue the fight and I need your support. People like you decide this work is worth funding, and it helps me continue! Without Arizona, roughly 70% of the statistical paths to the White House disappear. >> Whoever is the governor of Arizona will oversee the 2028 election. We need to win to secure the election. >> Arizona is the most consequential state in the presidential election. Lose it here, and 2028 gets a lot harder to win. >> Whoever wins the White House in 2028 runs the census. Whoever runs the census draws the lines for 2032. That's a decade of ground we don't get back. Here's how we win Arizona: We win by deploying real people, knocking on doors, building real relationships with real voters. It's having ballot chasers in the field every single day until Election Day. We've done it before. Our ballot chasers helped beat a Kamala-backed city councilwoman here in Arizona. They delivered a win in the Salt River Project race against a wall of environmental spending. And of course, it's how we delivered Arizona for Trump in 2028! This works. We've proven it works. Now we need to fund it at scale. Turning Point PAC is trying to raise $94,000 this week to put ballot chasers in the field across Arizona. body:
The federal government’s ardent promotion of “sex-rejecting”
medical procedures for minors during the Biden administration inspired
hundreds of hospitals and health care systems, many of them publicly
funded, to establish pediatric gender programs that made tens of
millions of dollars using illegal billing practices to get the
questionable treatments approved.

The federal government’s ardent promotion of “sex-rejecting”
medical procedures for minors during the Biden administration inspired
hundreds of hospitals and health care systems, many of them publicly
funded, to establish pediatric gender programs that made tens of
millions of dollars using illegal billing practices to get the
questionable treatments approved. More than 225 health care centers
established “pediatric gender programs,” billing nearly $120
million since 2019, according to an investigation conducted by the
Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). In a lengthy report
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85860&L=38827&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuaGhzLmdvdi9zaXRlcy9kZWZhdWx0L2ZpbGVzL2hocy13b2x2ZXMtaW4td2hpdGUtY29hdHMucGRmP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249Y29ycnVwdGlvbitjaHJvbmljbGVzJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE]&H=0604538be59d037886f19536ee810fbfa415b5f553bd6bd85517ede99ba86b57
made public recently the agency documents its findings and they are
downright outrageous. “This report exposes, for the first time, the
involvement of hospitals in promoting life-altering drugs and
surgeries for children who express discomfort with their sex,” HHS
writes. “The stories of young boys and girls who sought to
course-correct from the medical journeys designed to stunt and maim
their natural bodies and functions all tell the same tale: there was
no course-correction available.”
