Have you ever wondered what a battleground state looks like? Let me paint you a picture.
Vast plains. Rolling hills dotted with wild sunflowers. Wide fields of crops. Bustling cities and tight-knit small towns. Communities of folks looking out for their neighbors.
Sound familiar? Yes, I'm talking about Kansas.
Friends, this grassroots movement has turned Kansas into one of the most competitive Senate races in the nation.
Just this week, Nate Silver and now the Cook Political Report officially labeled our race a toss-up.
These are some of the most well-respected nonpartisan election analysts in the country, and they're telling us just how competitive this race really is. **They 're saying it'll come down to the wire on Election Day in under a month.**
But here's my promise to you. No matter how busy this campaign gets, I'll always make time to listen to Kansans. Because, for me, listening _is_ the work of a candidate and a Senator.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/4403a348-98c4-49fb-8995-893c759b1088?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
That's why, as this race heats up, I've spent every spare moment traveling across the great state of Kansas, meeting voters right where they are. I share my vision for Kansas (sometimes while standing on a bale of hay) -- and then I listen.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/4403a348-98c4-49fb-8995-893c759b1088?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Here's what's been incredible: In Kansas, we're already seeing the kind of team-playing and bridge-building that has become so rare in Washington. Folks here understand that this isn't about red vs. blue. It's about the future of our country. It's about giving hardworking families a fair shot in these challenging times. It's about giving Kansans a leader who will fight for _them_ , not special interests.
That's why I'm proud to have received endorsements from two Republican former Kansas governors over the past few weeks _and_ from Sen. Marshall's Republican primary challenger, who received 20% of the Republican vote in August.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/4403a348-98c4-49fb-8995-893c759b1088?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/4403a348-98c4-49fb-8995-893c759b1088?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This is exactly why I decided to run. I know my fellow Kansans. I know that we can rise above the divisiveness and cynicism that dominate politics today. I know we can lead with compassion and courage, not cruelty.
**The truth is, I 'm full of hope. Not just about the outcome of this race (we're neck-and-neck in the polls and truly can win this!), but about the future we can build for the next generation of Kansans.**
I joined this race for my granddaughter, Stella, and all the young people of Kansas. They're counting on us to leave this country better than we found it.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/4403a348-98c4-49fb-8995-893c759b1088?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/4403a348-98c4-49fb-8995-893c759b1088?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But while my faith in the people who make up this historic grassroots movement is unwavering, I also know how most races like these end up. I've seen the last 94 years of Kansas history, in which campaign after campaign has fallen short. I've watched how corporate PACs and special interests throw enough money at races like these to crush the momentum of hopeful movements like ours.
**Friends, we cannot let that happen in Kansas. That 's why I often end these Substack posts with an earnest ask to support my campaign. Too much is at stake to let our best chance to end the chaos and corruption in Washington slip away. [So please, if you're able, chip in today to power the truly remarkable future we're building in Kansas.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/4403a348-98c4-49fb-8995-893c759b1088?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) This close to Election Day, every dollar makes a difference.**
Let me end with this: There's another community I wish I could share a photo of -- the community of folks reading these messages, following our campaign virtually on our social media and pitching in to make all of this momentum possible. I'm truly grateful for each and every one of you for showing up in all the ways you can.
Have a beautiful Wednesday!
- Adam

Plus your Mountain Minute for 10/7/2026...

PRESENTED BY ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Hi friends!

We have a special edition today all around the ballot, which is likely
dropping into your mailbox any day now if it hasn't already. But if
you want the full news breakdown for today, listen to the Mountain
Minute podcast here
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
or watch on YouTube
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
or Rumble
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Mail ballots are landing in Colorado mailboxes this week, and this
year's ballot is a big one: 14 statewide measures, 13 of them put
there by citizens gathering signatures. Before you fill in a single
bubble, make sure your registration is current at GoVoteColorado.gov,
where you can check your status, update your address, and track your
ballot.

🛡️ SCAN IT. CHECK IT. PROTECT IT.

Moved in the last decade? Your old registration might still be sitting
on the rolls back where you left it. Heidi Ganahl is pointing voters
to a free tool from True the Vote at scancheckprotect.org.
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
In about two minutes, you can confirm your current registration is
right, make sure you're off the rolls everywhere you used to live, and
flag anything that looks wrong. Run it for yourself, then for your
parents and any kids who moved away for college.

WHAT'S ON YOUR 2026 COLORADO BALLOT: ALL 14 STATEWIDE MEASURES
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_Citizen petitions drove this year's ballot, and RMV breaks down every
question, who's behind it, and who's paying to stop it._

*
TWO TAX MEASURES ON A COLLISION COURSE: Amendment 87's graduated
income tax and Proposition 136's 4.4% rate cap pull in opposite
directions, and if both pass, majority of yes votes win... but it will
likely become a legal battle in courts if we get to that place.

*
OPPONENTS ARE OUTSPENDING ON KEY MEASURES: Coloradans for Real Safety
Solutions has raised about $1.1 million against Proposition 132's
fentanyl penalties, while Families Not Politics has raised $1.39
million against Propositions 134 and 135.

*
SPEAKING OF PROP 135: The Blue Book landing in your mailbox is
supposed to be the neutral guide to every measure, but former state
Sen. Kevin Lundberg says its Proposition 135 analysis reads like an
opposition handout
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
He argues the staff who prepared it, who answer to a committee the
legislative majority controls, ignored Protect Kids Colorado's input,
used loaded "gender-affirming" language, and relied on outdated 2019
data, so _VOTERS SHOULD READ IT WITH A CRITICAL EYE_.

*
PROP NN'S "2% FOR SCHOOLS" IS A CEILING: The Legislature's lone
referred measure would let the state keep TABOR surplus that would
otherwise be refunded (basically forever), with schools getting less
if the surplus shrinks

📅 KEY DATES

Oct. 9: Last day for county clerks to mail ballots to active voters
Oct. 12: All mail ballot drop boxes open
Oct. 19: Voting centers open for in-person voting and ballot drop-off
Oct. 26: Last recommended day to return your ballot by mail
Nov. 3: Election Day. Polls open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., and ballots must
reach county clerks by 7 p.m. to count
Nov. 12: Deadline for military and overseas ballots, and for fixing
signature discrepancies

This is your Mountain Minute for Wednesday, October 7, 2026.

– Team RMV

TODAY'S TOP STORIES

WHAT’S ON YOUR 2026 COLORADO BALLOT: ALL 14 STATEWIDE MEASURES
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY RMV EDITORIAL BOARD, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Colorado voters open their mail ballots this October to more
citizen-written questions than any election in half a century.

Fourteen measures. Thirteen put there by citizens gathering
signatures, one sent over by the Legislature. The total ties the
record set in 2024, 2008, and 2006, but the share driven by petition
rather than lawmakers sets this year apart.

Clerks began mailing ballots Oct. 2 and must have them out to every
active voter by Oct. 9. Election Day is Nov. 3.

Here is what each question does, who is behind it, and where the money
is. Committee registrations described below are those on file as of
Oct. 5. Campaign-finance figures reflect filings posted through Oct.
4. More committees can register before Election Day.

READ MORE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

LUNDBERG: PROPOSITION 135 GOT A BLUE BOOK HANDOUT FOR THE OPPOSITION
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY KEVIN LUNDBERG, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_A former state senator argues Colorado's official ballot guide failed
its nonpartisan mandate on Proposition 135, siding with opponents of
the measure to ban gender surgery on minors._

*
LOADED TERMINOLOGY, THE AUTHOR ARGUES: Lundberg says the Blue Book's
use of "gender-affirming surgery" assumes the outcome rather than
describing it neutrally, and contends more neutral language was
available but not used despite feedback from Protect Kids Colorado,
the group backing the measure.

*
OUTDATED DATA CITED AS EVIDENCE OF BIAS: The piece claims the Blue
Book relies on 2019 prevalence data that doesn't capture more recent
growth in these procedures, even after more current information was
reportedly provided to Legislative Council staff.

*
A FACTUAL DISPUTE OVER INSURANCE LANGUAGE: Lundberg argues the Blue
Book inaccurately states current law merely "allows" insurance to
cover these surgeries, when he contends state law actually requires
private insurance and state funding to cover them, outside self-funded
employer plans.

Peter, when
I say we desperately need a Democratic doctor in the U.S. Senate, I mean
it.

Just look at the record of the man running our country's health right now,
RFK Jr.:

* The diarrhea lettuce. Cyclospora, the "lettuce parasite," made
thousands of Michiganders sick this summer. RFK Jr. went on TV and
said it was under control while the case count kept climbing.
* Measles outbreaks. And all he's done is make it harder to get
vaccines.
* Constant food recalls. Our food's not any healthier because of him.

And the list goes on.

RFK Jr. came in promising to make America healthy. He had every chance to
stand up to the corporations putting additives in our food and pesticides
on our farms. He didn't, because he's bought off by the same corporations
that have been corrupting our food system for a very long time.

I don't take money from any corporations, so you can count on me to stand
up to them.

If I'm elected, I'd be the first Democratic doctor in the U.S. Senate
since 1969. I can't wait to sit across from RFK Jr. and hold him
accountable.

But first, we have to win in Michigan.

If Democrats want the majority, it runs through our race — and right now,
Republicans are spending $70 million to prop up a guy who will cheer RFK

_**Patriot**_ , I want to tell you something my daddy taught me back in my hometown of Jackson, Georgia. Buckle in, it’s a long story, and I’ve realized what it truly means after being on the campaign trail. He said Son, America isn’t just a place. _**It’s a promise**_. The promise that if you work hard, keep your head down, treat people right, and never quit, you can build something. **That’s the American Dream. ** And it’s the most powerful idea this world has ever seen. I watched it work in real time growing up in Jackson. I watched men and women with nothing but a strong back and a passion to put in the hours to build their businesses, raise their families, and leave something behind for their kids and grandkids. Isn’t that what life is about? Leaving the next generation better off than they found it? **That’s the America I fight for every day, Patriot. ** But here’s something I’ve found out going against Radical Socialist Jon Ossoff. The socialist movement is growing, y’all. And that scares the living daylights out of me.

clean_body: Mike Collins: The America I grew up in is worth every fight| | | Patriot , I want to tell you something my daddy taught me back in my hometown of Jackson, Georgia. Buckle in, it’s a long story, and I’ve realized what it truly means after being on the campaign trail. He said Son, America isn’t just a place. It’s a promise. The promise that if you work hard, keep your head down, treat people right, and never quit, you can build something. That’s the American Dream. And it’s the most powerful idea this world has ever seen. I watched it work in real time growing up in Jackson. I watched men and women with nothing but a strong back and a passion to put in the hours to build their businesses, raise their families, and leave something behind for their kids and grandkids. Isn’t that what life is about? Leaving the next generation better off than they found it? That’s the America I fight for every day, Patriot. But here’s something I’ve found out going against Radical Socialist Jon Ossoff. The socialist movement is growing, y’all. And that scares the living daylights out of me. The Democratic Party is no longer your daddy’s Democratic Party. They are undergoing a full-blown transformation into socialism. Jon Ossoff isn’t just going along for the ride; he is leading the charge. Think about what socialism actually means, Patriot. It means the government, not you, decides what you earn, what you keep, what your business is worth, and what your family deserves. It means the American Dream no longer belongs to the people who work for it. It belongs to Washington bureaucrats who have never run a business, never pulled a shift, never had grease under their fingernails, or laid awake at night wondering how to make payroll. It means the promise my daddy taught me, that promise that has powered this country for 250 years, gets quietly dismantled and replaced with government dependency, coastal elite control, and a Washington machine that decides your future for you. That is what Jon Ossoff is voting for every single time he shows up in that Senate chamber. And he is now posturing himself as the face of the Democrat Party’s socialist future heading into 2028. I’ll tell you what I believe in, but if this scares the heck out of you, as it does me, Patriot , I'm a trucker from Jackson, Georgia. I built a business from the cab of a rig. I know what the American Dream costs because I paid for it with early mornings, late nights, and years of grinding it out one mile at a time. And I will be absolutely damned if I am going to stand by and watch Jon Ossoff and the socialist wing of the Democrat Party dismantle that promise on my watch. I proudly stand with the brave men and women who have served our country, some even fighting against the spread of communism and had no clue it’d be taking over America. Listen here, I’m a normal person who worked my butt off to achieve the American Dream my daddy told me about. But here’s what this race has taught me. This race isn't just about a Senate seat. It isn't just about Georgia. It is about whether the America our founders built, the America where hard work means something, where freedom is real, where a kid from Jackson can grow up to drive trucks and then run for Senate, still exists on the other side of this election. I believe it can. I believe it's worth every fight, every mile, every prayer between now and November 3rd. But only if people like you are willing to stand up and say: NOT ON MY WATCH Today, , a nod to the year our founders made the most important declaration in human history. A declaration that this country belongs to its people. Not to socialist politicians who think they know better than you how to run your life. The American Dream is worth saving, Patriot. I've staked everything on it. Will you stand with me? subject: Philadelphia’s trash should not poison Chester
body:
The Reworld contract has been introduced. Tell the Philadelphia City Council and the Mayor to reject it. | |
---
Peter, **Philadelphia officials are trying to move forward with a waste contract that would keep sending the city’s trash to be burned in Chester. We’re escalating our campaign to stop them.** The City Council and the Mayor’s office have introduced the contract. That moves this decision closer to approval, with Philadelphia and Chester families left to bear the consequences of another agreement that pollutes our communities. Under Philadelphia’s previous waste contracts, roughly 40% of the city’s trash went to incinerators, most of it to Reworld’s Chester facility. Research presented to Pennsylvania lawmakers found that this facility emits more fine-particle pollution than any other trash incinerator _**in the country**_. It is a major source of air pollution across the whole Philadelphia region, contributing to above average asthma rates. Worse, in Chester, the incinerator has caused cancer and childhood asthma rates to more than double the average rate. **Chester and Philadelphia residents have spent decades organizing for clean air. The Philadelphia Mayor could now renew the toxic contract for 4 years, with a possible extension that stretches the arrangement to 7 years. This is not ok. Let's stop the contract before the city locks it in.** [**Tell the Philadelphia City Council and Mayor Cherelle Parker’s office to reject the Reworld contract and stop sending Philadelphia’s trash to be burned in Chester.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3_-6ezreVUDKM4uYMpG61B3tmZL107ueVKGrZcnb23wpIlNenMRc0EGDKYwCt9bDYoMDJMpGhP2LgFfCXKiSKRlKIdB9gTMnvhuAd1inXxcj4LeoEUydL_3jiA08U5wp77l065WAtucxEPl1jpAR003X3foqgbTSWN4mOkTb-D4Hd4tOwCogKRtIhNvpXnqiRZ8Xnax5kuoMAGch31xNEDxIyAgEBtVr4yZFcfCtzOB9DFHPVTNk49U0jAfOLy9-MaeaphsHarGUVPenaz_-V5FtbqJ5jQWf5n8UZ7-GqXYAkH39chpuPdlF2CsZNZVPOI/4uo/3LAl-dtFSaadMEMl9Ed_QQ/h0/h001.rM_33W2pg-ZFGjdvKrCd_KP5rx9k2Dwkx2JYLGHtT_0) | | [SIGN & SEND](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3_-6ezreVUDKM4uYMpG61B3tmZL107ueVKGrZcnb23wpLYdlLiQkASml6ohag1a_ds9UMAowi3DTV9ZnevzaPeqhMbbABW37K1tZsOs3uZDUPTjceZhPAQYq1iwuSB8mZQ2r5i1xjGFVIQMkOBHggL2RkdNZETiG_i0jVjaoQ7ZTzd-AOGP3Pl27HXQ1-VndKQ1G5TNmtBkH2ONqnW3-kl6tjOSJ7klPtiiwFU2exju-n1gNJEHuj4IhWnJDiE8HeTeapAywexLxTRH-PX3NfuED07g_J6y8PrJUbvJo1GCP1rKjZXB9wvA1zdCJYoE7UI/4uo/3LAl-dtFSaadMEMl9Ed_QQ/h1/h001.tDoljjabmIn67rkwHX1PkGCyNZ3fc34bkM0B2WMx97U)

Reworld spent more than $100,000 lobbying the City Council and the Parker administration while Philadelphia’s waste contracts were taking shape. The company has paid to put its interests in front of the people making this decision. We’re organizing to make sure those officials hear from the people living with the pollution.
**This is environmental racism carried out through public contracts. A majority-Black community is expected to absorb the pollution so another city can dispose of its waste and a corporation can keep collecting revenue.**
OnePA members are building power in Black and working-class communities to challenge decisions like this. Our neighbors’ health belongs at the center of public policy, and we’re bringing that demand directly to the City Council and the Mayor’s office.
The clock is ticking now that the contract has been introduced. **Whether you’re taking action for the first time or spoke out earlier, send a message today and help us turn up the pressure on both offices.**

The company has paid to put its interests in front of the people making this decision. We’re organizing to make sure those officials hear from the people living with the pollution. This is environmental racism carried out through public contracts. A majority-Black community is expected to absorb the pollution so another city can dispose of its waste and a corporation can keep collecting revenue. OnePA members are building power in Black and working-class communities to challenge decisions like this. Our neighbors’ health belongs at the center of public policy, and we’re bringing that demand directly to the City Council and the Mayor’s office. The clock is ticking now that the contract has been introduced. Whether you’re taking action for the first time or spoke out earlier, send a message today and help us turn up the pressure on both offices. | | Friend,

**Yesterday, I voted NO on another King County tax increase.**

The Council approved a new sales tax without sending it to voters, without a clear spending plan in place, and on the very same day we appointed a new Inspector General to root out corruption in programs similar to the one this tax is meant to fund.

**That 's not good enough for me. [Support my campaign _here_ if it's not good enough for you either!](https://us.list-manage.com/SxBkCrTbpcV?e=77eef70c61&c2id=352d4c3b964128868a59384c192ed166)**

Families across King County are struggling to afford housing, groceries, gas--and you guessed it--taxes! Government should not reach deeper into their pockets before proving it can responsibly manage the money it already has.
\------------------------------------------------------------
**_" Before asking King County families to once again pay more, we ought to get our own house in order." _
-Councilmember Reagan Dunn
[DONATE NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/2hGmaQpl4rf?e=77eef70c61&c2id=352d4c3b964128868a59384c192ed166)**
\------------------------------------------------------------

**[Read about my vote here | _MyNorthwest: King County Council approves sales tax increase without seeking voter approval_](https://us.list-manage.com/32mAxcSsMVC?e=77eef70c61&c2id=352d4c3b964128868a59384c192ed166)**

Thank you so much for your support! It motivates me to keep fighting the good fight _against_ higher taxes and _for_ a more affordable future when I know you [have my back](https://us.list-manage.com/WdnikDS0VnY?e=77eef70c61&c2id=352d4c3b964128868a59384c192ed166).

Like many of you, I’ve been deeply concerned that the rise of AI technology is outpacing regulation. It’s especially alarming to see leaders of frontier AI labs — who should themselves be doing more to protect the public — acknowledge that the current pace of model development is unsafe and that comprehensive regulation is essential. _The call is coming from inside the house. The danger is not theoretical anymore._ California has been a leader in the responsible regulation of AI, working to hold frontier AI labs under our existing consumer protection laws. People are organizing their communities across New York State and the country. **[Please click here to watch this special example from Ithaca, New York at the Southside Community Center:](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/39162?t=3&akid=12414%2E2526796%2EgI2V2K)**

Last week, I visited the Southside Community Center in Ithaca. This is how the world changes. It is in places like the Southside Community Center.
I know that things can feel scary right now but we have no other choice but to make this world a better place. I believe as long as we are gathering, creating community, and helping each other, a better world is inevitable. A world with Medicare for All, a living wage, and universal child care.

In solidarity,
Alexandria

subject: I'm not a fair-weather friend.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Elaine Luria for Congress
body:
This is for the women in uniform.

---

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: Abbott has spent ten times more money than us, but look at the polls.
body:
[1]LeftNet

Hi — it's Gina.

Everywhere I go in Texas, I hear the same thing: people are struggling in
ways they've never struggled before. Working people donating plasma before
their shift just to cover the bills. Families rationing insulin. Small
businesses closing because property taxes have gotten so out of hand.

And everywhere I go, I hear something else too: that this movement is
giving them hope. We’re closer than we’ve ever been before, but we have a
long way to go. People still worry if we can actually win here.

I understand that skepticism. Democrats have been saying Texas is turning
for years. But something is different now, and I need you to see the
numbers.

My campaign manager Amy put together a memo on exactly where this race
stands. Four independent polls now show us ahead. Abbott's own strategist
is admitting it will be close. Conservatives across Texas are crossing
over — on schools, on data centers, on the simple question of whether this
state belongs to the people or to Greg Abbott's billionaire donors.

[ https://act.leftnet.org/go/21583?c0=leftnet_em20261007_partner_ms_gh_em_leftnet.hJNcy3&refcode=em20261007-1719&t=1001&akid=1719%2E2118727%2EofQzS5 ]Read the memo. Then, if you believe what I believe — that we can
actually win this — I'm asking you to pitch in whatever you can.

[ https://act.leftnet.org/go/21450?c0=leftnet_em20261007_partner_ms_gh_em_leftnet.y5ZyZw&refcode=em20261007-1719&amount=5&t=1002&akid=1719%2E2118727%2EofQzS5 ]DONATE ››

=============================================================

OCTOBER 2026 CAMPAIGN MEMO ON TX-GOV

FROM: Amy Friedman, Campaign Manager, Gina for Texas
TO: Interested Parties

Let me tell you where this race actually stands — because what's happening
in Texas right now is something I don't think the national establishment
fully understands yet.

Gina Hinojosa is leading Greg Abbott in four of the most recent polls.
That’s never happened before.

This race is closer than ever but some people still don’t believe we can
win — that’s exactly why I'm writing this memo. And it's exactly why this
race could slip away if we don't act.

Here's the polling picture. This race has moved steadily and dramatically
in Gina's direction since the spring:

* Texas Politics Project (April 2026): Abbott +5
* TPOR (July 2026): Abbott +3, inside the margin of error
* N+ Univision (September 9): Tied 47–47, with Gina leading Latino
voters by 12
* ReconMR/Siena (September 17): Gina leads 49–45 — independents breaking
for Gina 65–27
* NPR/Marist (September 23): Gina leads 49–46, winning independents
52–39, pulling 9% of self-identified Republicans
* NYT/Siena (October 4): Gina leads 49–46, winning independents 55–39,
and leading among Latino voters by 31 points

Both RealClearPolitics and Nate Silver's Silver Bulletin have the polling
average under 2 points. This is a toss-up.

Abbott is outspending us 10 to 1 — and he still isn’t getting the result
he wants.

Between July 30 and September 8 alone, Abbott outspent Gina $28 million to
$2 million on advertising. Over the full race, he's spent $47 million to
our $5 million. Despite that, Gina leads in four of the most recent polls.
Abbott's favorability has gone deeply negative — 45% favorable, 53%
unfavorable — and his job approval has flipped the same way. He's even
polling 13% unfavorable among his own Republicans.

Abbott is a damaged incumbent with a nine-figure war chest. The only thing
keeping this race from breaking open is the spending gap.

But here’s the truth: The more money Abbott spends lying about Gina’s
record, the more vulnerable we are. We have to raise more money to reach
the voters who haven’t heard from us yet.

Something real is happening on the ground — and Republicans know it.

Lifelong conservative voters are publicly breaking with Abbott over two
issues.

On education: conservative moms who backed Abbott before are now appearing
at Gina's events, frustrated by a decade of voucher schemes and defunded
public schools. Gina is running an ad featuring a self-described MAGA
conservative who protested on January 6 — and is now voting for Gina
because of schools.

On data centers: rural Republican protest groups — including one in
Lubbock led by Republicans — are furious about unregulated expansion
driving up electricity bills. Abbott championed data centers for years,
took millions from their developers, and is now scrambling to reverse
course. Gina called for a moratorium from day one.

As Gina put it to The Nation: The data-center issue is the latest example
of a governor doing the bidding of moneyed interests and not the people of
Texas. And it is angering MAGA Republicans — not country-club Republicans,
not Chamber of Commerce Republicans. There is an opportunity for alliances
to be forged when we are pursuing a populist agenda.

Even Abbott's own team is admitting this race is close.

Abbott's longtime political strategist was asked about the tightening
polls. His response: "Is it going to be close on Election Day? Yes."
That’s Abbott's own guy publicly conceding this goes to the wire. And when
pressed on his best argument against Gina? He went to culture wars and
lies on income tax votes — not data centers, not schools, not the
affordability crisis Abbott has presided over for twelve years. When
culture wars are the best attack you can come up with, you're losing
ground.

The coalition winning this race doesn't look like past Texas Democratic
coalitions.

Gina leads independents by 38 points in the Siena poll. She's winning
women 57–40%, voters under 45 by 60–33%, and Gen Z 71–19%. She's pulling
9% of self-identified Republicans. In TX-15 — a district Trump carried
58–41 — a House Majority PAC poll shows Gina leading 52–47.

time. Gina is earning support from Texans who have never voted for a
Democrat before in their lives.

energy flipped 12 State House seats, 2 State Senate seats, and 2
congressional seats. And the stakes this cycle go even further: if Abbott
wins another term, Republicans will redraw the congressional map again.

or ten congressional seats permanently out of Democratic reach — one-party
control of Congress, likely for a generation. A governor who vetoes rigged
maps changes all of that. As Gina said: "We flip Texas, and it's over."

favorability and approval. Conservatives are crossing over to support our
campaign. The polling average is under 2 points. Abbott's own strategist
admits this race will be close.

try to buy his lead back in the final few weeks of this race.

in Texas right now — and decide this race is worth their investment.

Hi Fellow American - it's Michele.
Wow. The first few weeks since I launched my run for U.S. Senate have been a whirlwind! I've done as many interviews, press events, and TV hits as I possibly could to spread the word about what we're trying to do here:
1\. Clean up the mess that the political class has left us in 2\. Hold our corrupt leaders who sold us out to account 3\. Retake this Minnesota Senate seat in the name of sanity
I hope that plan resonates with you.
Between the hustle and bustle of a new campaign, I just wanted to personally reach out and thank you for your support thus far.
This race will be won or lost in the margins. Every prayer, every dollar given, and even you just taking the time to read this email means a great deal to me. I mean that.
I'm not a politician, and I'll never take your support for granted.
I want you to feel a part of this team - because you are. When we beat the odds and flip this seat, it'll be your victory too.
